justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: Clinical practice reports positive; formal comparative studies vs standard feeding therapy absent.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: 2-day workshop; moderate cost; accessible to SLP and OT practitioners.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applicable in pediatric feeding programs; relevant for SLP and OT in pediatric medical and school settings.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: Billed under feeding therapy SLP/OT codes; certification supports medical necessity documentation; commercial and Medicaid coverage apply.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Moderate employer demand in pediatric feeding programs and feeding specialty clinics.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Family-centered, non-coercive approach reduces mealtime anxiety for families.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Parents of picky/ARFID kids routinely pay cash when insurance won't cover feeding therapy; strong direct-pay market.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: Specialized feeding clinics command premium rates and often have waitlists.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Named brand approach with limited certified provider pool; strong differentiation in pediatric markets.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Multiple trained SLPs/OTs can deliver SOS within a clinic; genuinely scalable to a multi-clinician practice.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Growing parent awareness via social media and pediatrician referrals, though still niche.
justifications.business.efficiency: Reasonable course-based training (8-day conference + mentorship); accessible compared to multi-year credentials.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Recognized in pediatric SLP/OT academic circles but not a board specialty; moderate hiring signal for peds faculty.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Some published outcomes work but evidence base is debated; modest scholarly output.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Directly applicable to pediatric feeding coursework in SLP and OT programs.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Evidence is largely program-developer driven with limited independent RCTs.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Occasionally preferred for pediatric SLP/OT faculty positions, especially with feeding clinic affiliations.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Relatively quick to obtain compared to residencies, with decent academic payoff in peds programs.
